papers.title: Melatonin-loaded proniosomes enhance gemcitabine response in gemcitabine-resistant cholangiocarcinoma: Proteomic and computational insights.
papers.abstract: Acquired resistance to gemcitabine (GEM) remains a major barrier in cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) therapy. Melatonin has multi-targeted antitumor activity but is limited by rapid elimination and low oral bioavailability. We developed a maltodextrin-based melatonin-loaded proniosome (MPN) and evaluated its physicochemical properties, ex vivo permeation, and antitumor activity, alone and with GEM, in a GEM-resistant CCA model. MPN was prepared by a provesicular slurry method and characterized for physicochemical properties, stability, molecular dynamics (MD), and ex vivo permeation. Efficacy and tole
papers.summary: Researchers developed a maltodextrin-based melatonin-loaded proniosome (MPN) formulation to overcome melatonin's poor bioavailability and tested it, alone and combined with gemcitabine, in a gemcitabine-resistant cholangiocarcinoma model. The formulation improved melatonin delivery and, combined with proteomic and computational analyses, enhanced the antitumor response to gemcitabine in resistant cells. The work suggests a nanomedicine strategy to reverse chemoresistance in bile duct cancer.

papers.title: Exploring the role and mechanism of methionine metabolism in chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps based on bioinformatics analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic Rhinosinusitis with Nasal Polyps (CRSwNP) affects 1%-4% of the global population with high recurrence rates. While methionine metabolism abnormalities contribute to various inflammatory diseases, their role in CRSwNP pathogenesis remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically investigate the role of methionine metabolism in CRSwNP and identify potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets through integrating multi-omics data and interpretable machine learning approaches.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with interpretable machine learning to investigate how abnormal methionine metabolism contributes to chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP), a common inflammatory condition with high recurrence rates. The authors aim to identify methionine-metabolism-related biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets for the disease.

papers.title: Identifying phase separation modulators mediated by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein using a structure-based drug discovery approach.
papers.abstract: As severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) continues to evolve through mutations and acquire resistance to existing antiviral agents, the persistence of post-pandemic infections remains a significant global health concern. To address these challenges, it is crucial to develop novel therapeutic agents that target previously unexplored viral or host mechanisms.
papers.summary: This study uses a structure-based drug discovery approach to identify small molecules that modulate phase separation driven by the SARS-CoV-2 nucleocapsid protein, a viral mechanism not targeted by current antivirals. The work aims to uncover new therapeutic candidates that could remain effective despite viral mutation and resistance to existing drugs.

papers.title: Unlocking the electronic and adsorption origin of doping-engineered WS2 monolayers: a DFT investigation with machine learning validation.
papers.abstract: Defect-engineered tungsten disulfide (WS2) monolayers provide a tunable platform for clarifying how local dopant chemistry that converts weak gas adsorption into measurable electronic perturbation. Here, N-doped and N-O co-doped WS2 monolayers are investigated to decouple adsorption strength from electronic-response descriptors toward CO, CO2, and NH3 sensing. Machine learning force field (MLFF)-assisted DFT calculations show that MLFF reproduces the DFT energy-force relationships and phonon trends for pristine WS2 and N-WS2, whereas the larger deviations for N-O-WS2 indicate that co-doped con
papers.summary: This study uses DFT calculations, validated by a machine-learning force field, to examine how nitrogen doping and nitrogen-oxygen co-doping of WS2 monolayers change their electronic response and adsorption behavior toward CO, CO2, and NH3 gases. The MLFF reproduces DFT energetics and phonon trends well for pristine and N-doped WS2, but shows larger deviations for the co-doped system, suggesting limits to its transferability. The work aims to separate adsorption strength from electronic-response descriptors for gas sensing applications.

papers.title: General prediction of T cell receptor antigen specificity from sequence using AlphaFold 3.
papers.abstract: The major histocompatibility complex (MHC):peptide:T cell receptor (TCR) complex is the most diverse trimolecular interface known in nature and a key trigger for adaptive immunity. TCRs are now routinely sequenced at scale; however, decoding their specificity for antigens remains a bottleneck. While in silico approaches have advanced considerably, none enables prediction against "unseen" epitopes, limiting their applicability to a tiny fraction of cases. Here, we show that AlphaFold 3 (AF3) predicts the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy. By applying AF3 to >9000
papers.summary: The authors show that AlphaFold 3 can predict the structures of MHC:peptide:TCR triads with unprecedented accuracy, and by applying it to over 9,000 complexes they build a model that predicts TCR antigen specificity even for epitopes not seen during training. This addresses a major bottleneck in immunology, since TCRs are sequenced at scale but decoding which antigen each recognizes has remained largely infeasible for unseen epitopes.

papers.title: Aspergillus terreus MAK153 against Fusarium oxysporum: biocontrol, metabolites, and simvastatin docking.
papers.abstract: This study demonstrates the considerable antagonistic activity of Aspergillus terreus MAK153 against a pathogenic Fusarium oxysporum AUMC3191 isolate. In dual culture assay, soil-isolated Aspergillus terreus Thom effectively hindered F. oxysporum AUMC3191 growth and impressively blocked zearalenone (ZEN) synthesis. Scanning electron microscopy demonstrated significant damage to F. oxysporum hyphae, such as abnormalities, shrinkage, bending, and deformity. Molecular identification through rDNA ITS sequence analysis confirmed the isolate as Aspergillus terreus, registered in GeneBank (Accession
papers.summary: The soil-derived fungus Aspergillus terreus MAK153 strongly inhibited growth of the plant pathogen Fusarium oxysporum in dual-culture assays and blocked its production of the mycotoxin zearalenone, with electron microscopy showing clear hyphal damage. The authors identified the isolate by ITS sequencing and used metabolite profiling plus molecular docking of simvastatin to explore the antifungal mechanism. The work supports A. terreus as a potential biocontrol agent against Fusarium wilt and mycotoxin contamination.

papers.title: ARIEL: an openly accessible database of experimental RNA-ligand binding affinities paired with 3D structures.
papers.abstract: RNA is an increasingly attractive target for small-molecule therapeutics, yet the rational design and computational modelling of RNA-binding small molecules are constrained by the scarcity of experimentally measured binding affinities linked to 3D structures. Here we present ARIEL (Affinity Resource for Interactions of RNA and Ligands), an openly accessible, manually curated database that pairs experimentally determined dissociation constants (Kd) of RNA-ligand complexes with the corresponding experimental structures. We screened 6954 RNA-containing structures from the Protein Data Bank, extra
papers.summary: ARIEL is a new, openly accessible database that manually curates experimentally measured RNA-ligand binding affinities (Kd values) and pairs them with the corresponding 3D structures from the Protein Data Bank. By screening 6,954 RNA-containing structures, the resource addresses the scarcity of linked affinity-structure data that has limited rational design and computational modeling of RNA-binding small molecules. It provides a foundational dataset for structure-based drug discovery targeting RNA.

papers.title: Synthesis, molecular structure, supramolecular and biological evaluation of benzimidazole-based Schiff bases.
papers.abstract: Benzimidazole-based Schiff bases, (Z)-2-(((1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)imino)methyl)phenol monohydrate (HL1·H2O) and (Z)-1-(((1H-benzo[d]imidazol-2-yl)imino)methyl)naphthalen-2-ol monohydrate (HL2·H2O) were synthesized and characterized by IR, UV-vis, EI-mass, 1H NMR spectroscopy, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies. Molecular structure determination suggested the presence of crystal water in the unit cell of each compound. The structure adopted a usual enol-imine form, with an intramolecular hydrogen bond between the phenolate-oxygen and the imine-nitrogen atoms. Supramolecular packing
papers.summary: Two benzimidazole-based Schiff base compounds were synthesized and fully characterized, including by single-crystal X-ray diffraction, revealing enol-imine tautomers with intramolecular hydrogen bonding and water molecules in the crystal lattice. The study also examines their supramolecular packing and reports biological evaluation of the compounds. This is a routine synthetic/structural chemistry contribution with limited broader relevance to bioinformatics.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into the metabolomic profiling and anticancer potential of Paspalum dilatatum in breast cancer: integrated phytochemical, in vitro, and in silico studies.
papers.abstract: The study explored the metabolite profile and anticancer potential of Paspalum dilatatum (Dallis grass) using an integrated phytochemical, computational, and in vitro approach. UHPLC/QTOF-MS/MS analysis of a 70% methanolic extract tentatively identified 30 metabolites, mainly flavonoids. In vitro MTT assays showed dose-dependent cytotoxicity against breast cancer MCF7 cells (IC50 = 73.70 µg mL-1) and liver cancer HEPG2 cells (IC50 = 128.02 µg mL-1), with high selectivity over normal Vero cells (p < 0.0001). Mechanistic studies in MCF7 cells demonstrated apoptosis induction, as supported by inc
papers.summary: This study profiled the metabolites of Dallis grass (Paspalum dilatatum) using mass spectrometry, identifying 30 compounds (mostly flavonoids), and tested the extract against breast and liver cancer cell lines. The extract showed dose-dependent cytotoxicity with selectivity for cancer cells over normal cells, and mechanistic experiments in MCF7 breast cancer cells indicated apoptosis induction. The work combines phytochemical profiling, in vitro assays, and computational (in silico) analysis to suggest anticancer potential.

papers.title: Ebola Virus VP40 C-terminal Lysine Residue Mediates Lipid Interactions and Dimer-Dimer Interactions.
papers.abstract: The Ebola virus (EBOV) matrix protein VP40 is the main driver of viral assembly and budding, processes which depend on its ability to oligomerize at the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane (PM). VP40 forms dimers in the cytoplasm that traffic to the membrane and assemble into higher-order oligomers, but the specific molecular determinants governing the stability of these oligomeric interfaces are not fully understood. Here, we investigate the role of the C-terminal lysine residue, Lys326, in mediating VP40-lipid and VP40-VP40 interactions. Using a combination of molecular dynamics simulations
papers.summary: This study investigates how a single C-terminal lysine residue (Lys326) in the Ebola virus matrix protein VP40 contributes to the protein's ability to bind lipid membranes and to assemble into higher-order oligomers. Using molecular dynamics simulations, the authors show that Lys326 mediates both VP40-lipid interactions and dimer-dimer contacts, helping explain how VP40 drives viral assembly and budding at the plasma membrane.

papers.title: Harnessing engineered laccase and functional carrier materials for efficient dye degradation: From mechanism to application.
papers.abstract: Laccases are copper-containing oxidases that have been widely investigated for the decolorization and degradation of synthetic dyes, including azo, anthraquinone, triphenylmethane, indigo and thiazine dyes. However, their application in dye-containing wastewater remains constrained by enzyme instability under complex effluent conditions, limited oxidation of some recalcitrant or high-redox-potential dyes, mediator dependence, and poor recovery and reuse of free laccase. This review discusses recent progress in laccase-catalyzed dye degradation from a mechanism-to-engineering perspective, linki
papers.summary: This review examines how engineered laccases combined with functional carrier materials can improve the degradation of synthetic dyes in wastewater. It covers the catalytic mechanisms of laccase-mediated dye breakdown and engineering strategies to overcome enzyme instability, limited substrate range, mediator dependence, and poor reusability of free enzyme.

papers.title: Computational and experimental study of CuO-ZnO nanocomposite using the plant Peganum harmala L. and their antifungal, antibacterial applications.
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of AMR necessitates the development of novel, sustainable therapeutic agents. This study reports the green synthesis of copper-decorated zinc oxide (CuO-ZnO) nanocomposite using an aqueous leaf extract of Peganum harmala L., which served as a reducing and capping agent. A quantitative EDX analysis confirmed a high loading of Cu of 24.25% (7.09%) mass. Characterization showed that the average primary particle size was 29 ± 1.3 nm, and that the structures were crystalline and hexagonal, known as wurtzite. The nanocomposite exhibited a positive zeta potential of + 47.2 ± 4.24
papers.summary: The authors synthesized a CuO-ZnO nanocomposite using an aqueous leaf extract of Peganum harmala as a green reducing and capping agent, producing crystalline wurtzite particles of ~29 nm with 24% copper loading and a positive surface charge. The material was characterized and evaluated for antibacterial and antifungal activity, positioning it as a potential sustainable alternative in the fight against antimicrobial resistance.

papers.title: Wrapping mechanism of β-lactoglobulin around SDS micelles characterized by time-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet circular dichroism and molecular dynamics simulation.
papers.abstract: Conformational transitions of water-soluble proteins at membrane interfaces play an important role in biological functions and diseases. Herein, we present a novel analytical framework capable of revealing the unique stepwise wrapping of β-lactoglobulin (bLG) around anionic sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) micelles by integrating time-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet circular dichroism (TR-VUVCD) spectroscopy with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. TR-VUVCD spectra of bLG interacting with SDS micelles were measured over 0.4-90 s, revealing that this interaction induces a β-to-α conformational transit
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.summary: This study combines time-resolved vacuum-ultraviolet circular dichroism spectroscopy with molecular dynamics simulations to resolve how β-lactoglobulin wraps around anionic SDS micelles over a 0.4–90 second timescale. The interaction drives a stepwise β-to-α conformational transition in the protein, revealing a detailed wrapping mechanism at membrane-like interfaces. The work offers a new analytical framework for studying protein conformational changes at membrane interfaces.

papers.title: Tyrosinase-SWCNT Electrochemical Biosensor for Tyramine Detection: Experimental Development and Molecular Dynamics Insights.
papers.abstract: Tyramine (TYM) serves as a critical indicator of microbial spoilage and significant health risks at elevated concentrations. Herein, we report an integrated experimental and computational approach to develop a high-performance electrochemical biosensor for selective TYM detection. Tyrosinase (Tyro) was immobilized onto carboxylated single-walled carbon nanotube-modified screen-printed carbon electrodes (Tyro-COOH-SWCNT/SPCE) to construct a nanostructured bioelectrode. The resulting biosensor exhibits a detection limit of 1.15 × 10-6 M and a linear range from 9.98 × 10-6 to 1.08 × 10-4 M. Furth
papers.summary: This paper describes an electrochemical biosensor for detecting tyramine, a compound that signals microbial food spoilage and poses health risks at high levels. The sensor immobilizes the enzyme tyrosinase on carboxylated single-walled carbon nanotubes deposited on screen-printed carbon electrodes, achieving a detection limit of about 1.15 µM over a linear range of roughly 10–108 µM. Molecular dynamics simulations complement the experiments to explain how the enzyme interacts with the nanotube-modified surface.

papers.title: Salt Effects on the Growth of Mixed Anionic and Zwitterionic Surfactant Micelles.
papers.abstract: We investigate the changes in 3:1 mixed sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) and cocamidopropyl betaine (CAPB) surfactant solutions (at the 400 mM scale) upon addition of alkali/halide salts up to a concentration of 2.5 M using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations coupled with a Hamiltonian replica exchange scheme and accounting for long-range electrostatic effects. Upon addition of salt, micelle properties (size, morphology, degree of neutralization, equilibrium between surfactant chains within 'end-cap' and 'cylindrical' micellar subdomains) as well as surfactant solution shear viscosities
papers.summary: This study uses coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations with Hamiltonian replica exchange to examine how added alkali/halide salts affect 3:1 mixed SDS/CAPB surfactant micelles at high concentration. Salt addition alters micelle size, morphology, charge neutralization, and the balance of surfactant chains between end-cap and cylindrical subdomains, with corresponding changes in solution shear viscosity. The work provides a computational framework for predicting salt-driven micelle behavior in mixed anionic-zwitterionic surfactant systems.

papers.title: Simulating Directed Evolution In Silico with an Iterative, Physics-Based Workflow.
papers.abstract: Directed evolution consistently delivers engineered enzymes that facilitate diverse biocatalytic transformations. Despite advances in automation and high-throughput workflows, our ability to rapidly engineer novel enzymes is limited by our inability to thoroughly sample the vast protein design space. Generative artificial intelligence (AI) methods have alleviated this challenge to some degree, due to their ability to propose mutations based on learned patterns from complex protein data sets. However, the hidden logic of these AI-based methods can complicate our ability to reveal and exploit fu
papers.summary: The paper presents an iterative, physics-based computational workflow that simulates directed evolution in silico to engineer enzymes. Unlike generative AI methods that rely on learned patterns and are often opaque, this approach uses physics-based modeling to propose and evaluate mutations, aiming to sample protein design space more thoroughly and interpretably. The work addresses the challenge of rapidly engineering novel enzymes by providing a transparent alternative to black-box AI-driven protein design.

papers.title: Degradation Behavior of NBR Seals Exposed to Halogenated Olefins under Coupled Thermal and Mechanical Loads: A Multiscale Experimental and Computational Study.
papers.abstract: Halogenated olefins are promising low-GWP substitutes for traditional halocarbons in refrigeration, fire protection, and energy storage, but their compatibility with elastomeric seals poses a potential safety risk in process systems. This study systematically investigates the degradation behavior of nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) exposed to five representative halogenated olefins-namely, 2-bromo-3,3,3-trifluoropropene (2-BTP), 2-chloro-3,3,3-trifluoropropene (R1233xf), 2,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234yf), cis-1,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R1234ze-(Z)), and trans-1,3,3,3-tetrafluoropropene (R123
papers.summary: This study examines how nitrile butadiene rubber (NBR) seals degrade when exposed to five halogenated olefin refrigerants under combined heat and mechanical stress, using both experiments and computational modeling. It characterizes the chemical and physical deterioration of the seals across multiple scales to assess compatibility and safety risks in refrigeration and energy systems. The work provides practical guidance on material selection for low-GWP refrigerant applications.

papers.title: Optimization and Application of ReaxFF for the Aqueous Carbonation of Calcium Silicates in Steel Slag.
papers.abstract: The existing ReaxFF for the C/H/O/Ca/Si system exhibits poor compatibility with aqueous multiphase reactions. In this work, the aqueous carbonation of dicalcium silicate (C2S) derived from steel slag was selected as the research system, and parameter optimization and validation of the reactive force field were performed. Density functional theory with the GGA-PBE functional was adopted to conduct structural relaxation and potential energy surface scanning for C2S polymorphs, carbonate species, and reaction intermediates, and a comprehensive structure-energy training data set was established. S
papers.summary: This paper optimizes the ReaxFF reactive force field for simulating the aqueous carbonation of dicalcium silicate (C2S) from steel slag, a key reaction in CO2 mineralization. The authors used DFT (GGA-PBE) to build a training set of structures and energies for C2S polymorphs, carbonate species, and intermediates, then reparameterized the force field to better handle multiphase aqueous reactions. The optimized ReaxFF is validated and applied to model the carbonation process, improving the reliability of molecular simulations for this system.

papers.title: Discovery and Design of YTHDF2-Selective and Pan-YTHDF Inhibitors for m6A Binding by the YTH Aromatic Cage.
papers.abstract: Recognition of N6-methyl-adenosine (m6A) in the RNA sequences by the YT521-B homology domain-containing protein family paralogs 1-3 (YTHDF1-3) is a dominant layer of myriad cellular regulation. Dysregulated YTHDF paralog expression and activities have been reported in cancer, including glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) in which YTHDF2 has been identified as a druggable dependency. Guided by structure-based in silico screening, we identified structurally related small-molecule compound families of promising YTHDF inhibitor compounds. Following in vitro screening, two hits, DT11 and DT15, emerged an
papers.summary: This study uses structure-based virtual screening to discover small-molecule inhibitors that target the m6A-binding aromatic cage of YTHDF proteins, yielding hits DT11 and DT15. The compounds show selectivity for YTHDF2 as well as pan-YTHDF activity, offering chemical probes for dissecting m6A reader function and potential leads for cancers such as glioblastoma where YTHDF2 is a druggable dependency.

papers.title: Substrate recognition and stage-dependent transformation of aflatoxin B1 by mediator-free Bacillus laccase frL103.
papers.abstract: Enzyme-based mitigation of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is commonly evaluated by parent-toxin depletion. This study characterized the stage-dependent, mediator-free transformation of AFB1 by recombinant Bacillus laccase frL103 and assessed chemical, biological, and structural outcomes. UHPLC-HRMS profiling at 0, 30, and 60 h yielded 2846 filtered features and showed that the AFB1 response decreased to 23.8% and 14.8% of the initial value at 30 and 60 h, respectively. A feature at m/z 329.0660 increased at 30 h and declined to 17.7% of that response at 60 h; accurate mass and MS/MS fragmentation support
papers.summary: This study characterizes how a recombinant Bacillus laccase (frL103) degrades aflatoxin B1 without requiring a mediator, tracking the reaction over 60 hours by mass spectrometry. AFB1 levels dropped to about 24% and 15% of initial at 30 and 60 hours, while an intermediate feature at m/z 329.0660 rose then declined, indicating a stage-dependent transformation pathway rather than simple depletion. The work highlights that parent-toxin loss alone is an incomplete measure of detoxification.

papers.title: Bisphenol A induces ACSL4-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury: Implications for Hunner-type interstitial cystitis.
papers.abstract: Hunner-type interstitial cystitis (HIC) is an inflammatory subtype of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome marked by persistent urothelial injury and bladder dysfunction. Bisphenol A (BPA) can disturb redox and inflammatory homeostasis, but its relevance to HIC-associated urothelial vulnerability remains unclear. This study examined whether acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) contributes to BPA-associated ferro-aging-like urothelial injury. Among non-pregnant adult women, higher creatinine-corrected urinary BPA was associated with a phenotype predominantly characteriz
papers.summary: This study links bisphenol A (BPA) exposure to urothelial injury resembling ferroptosis and cellular aging, mediated by the lipid-metabolism enzyme ACSL4, and proposes this as a mechanism relevant to Hunner-type interstitial cystitis. In a human cohort, higher urinary BPA was associated with a phenotype consistent with this injury pattern, and mechanistic experiments implicate ACSL4 in the process.

papers.title: On the limits of marginal protein folding stability: methodological goals and drawbacks.
papers.abstract: Why do proteins remain at the edge of stability rather than evolving toward maximal thermodynamic robustness? Can we trust the computational methods that inform about when and how stability falls off that edge? Marginal stability, the confinement of protein folding free energies to a window of approximately 5-15 kcal/mol, is broadly observed in biophysics, and its mechanistic causes, involving evolutionary and biophysical properties, remain under debate and require accurate predictions. In this regard, protein folding stability is currently predicted using both traditional structure-based homo
papers.summary: This paper critically examines why proteins evolve to be only marginally stable (folding free energies of ~5-15 kcal/mol) rather than maximally stable, and evaluates whether computational methods used to predict folding stability are reliable. It discusses the methodological goals and limitations of structure-based and other stability prediction approaches, highlighting the need for accurate predictions to understand the evolutionary and biophysical causes of marginal stability.

papers.title: Comparative Analysis of Relative Ligand Binding Free Energy Simulation Methods: Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD.
papers.abstract: Structure-based drug design has become increasingly important in the pharmaceutical industry for accelerating the discovery of effective drug candidates. In particular, ligand binding free energy serves as a critical metric for predicting drug efficacy during the key stages of hit discovery and lead optimization. Continuous progress has been made in the prediction of ligand binding free energies, but direct comparisons of different methods using the same force field remain challenging due to their unique implementations in different simulation engines. In this study, we present a direct compar
papers.journal: Journal of chemical theory and computation
papers.summary: This study directly compares four relative ligand binding free energy simulation methods (Amber-TI, GROMACS-NETI, OpenMM-FEP, and BLaDE-MSLD) using the same force field, overcoming the usual barrier of differing implementations across simulation engines. The comparison provides a benchmark of accuracy and performance across these approaches for structure-based drug design applications like hit discovery and lead optimization.

papers.title: SynBioFooDB: a comprehensive resource for synthetic biology-driven food biomanufacturing.
papers.abstract: Enabled by synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, microbial biomanufacturing is reshaping the production of food-related compounds by offering sustainable alternatives to resource-intensive extraction and conventional chemical synthesis. However, information linking food-related compounds to biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence remains fragmented across the literature and poorly represented in existing food-oriented resources, hindering cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems. Here, we present SynBioFooDB (h
papers.summary: SynBioFooDB is a new database that links food-related compounds to their biosynthetic pathways and microbial biomanufacturing evidence, addressing the fragmentation of this information across literature and existing food resources. It aims to enable cross-study comparison, evidence synthesis, and rational design of microbial production systems for food compounds.

papers.title: DockBind: A Quality-Controlled Data Set of Modeled Protein-Ligand Complexes Associated with Affinity Data.
papers.abstract: Ligand-protein interaction prediction is essential for structure-based drug discovery, but further development of machine-learning scoring functions is limited by a lack of high-quality training data sets. Here, we present DockBind, a curated data set of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, generated through a quality-controlled docking workflow. This workflow was developed based on an expanded docking benchmark, where we systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods as well as ligand similarity and maximum common substructure (MCS
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: DockBind is a curated dataset of modeled protein-ligand complexes paired with experimental binding affinity data, built using a quality-controlled docking workflow. The authors systematically evaluated free and template-based docking methods, ligand similarity, and maximum common substructure approaches on an expanded benchmark to develop this workflow. The dataset aims to address the shortage of high-quality training data that limits machine-learning scoring functions for structure-based drug discovery.

papers.title: A piperamide natural compound is compatible with an inactive DFG-out conformation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2: In silico and in vitro model study.
papers.abstract: Vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 (VEGFR2) is a well-known key regulator of angiogenic cancers. In a structure-based virtual screening of Indonesian natural compounds, dehydropipernonaline (DPN), a piperamide from Piper species, emerged as a promising VEGFR2-binding candidate. However, its inhibitory activity against VEGFR2 has not been experimentally validated. This study combined molecular simulations and cellular assays to investigate the potential interaction between DPN and VEGFR2. Molecular docking predicted that DPN occupies the regulatory domain pocket (RDP) spanning the ca
papers.summary: This study used structure-based virtual screening to identify dehydropipernonaline (DPN), a piperamide from Piper species, as a candidate VEGFR2 binder, then validated it with molecular simulations and cellular assays. Docking predicted DPN occupies the regulatory domain pocket and is compatible with an inactive DFG-out conformation of VEGFR2. The work provides in silico and in vitro evidence supporting DPN as a potential anti-angiogenic compound, though further optimization and in vivo validation are needed.

papers.title: Small genomes, big lessons: What viruses teach us about structure-based riboregulation.
papers.abstract: RNA viruses encode multiple layers of information within a single molecule, which functions simultaneously as a template for protein synthesis and as a structured regulatory RNA. These structures control key aspects of viral gene expression, govern host interactions, and mediate immune evasion. Although the prevalence of RNA structure in viral genomes is now well established, only recently have functional and mechanistic studies begun to uncover how these elements act as regulatory modules that shape infection outcomes. With their compact genomes and experimentally tractable life cycles, RNA v
papers.summary: This review discusses how RNA viruses pack regulatory information into structured RNA elements within their compact genomes, using the same RNA molecule both as a protein-coding template and as a structured regulator. It highlights recent functional and mechanistic work showing how these RNA structures control viral gene expression, host interactions, and immune evasion, and argues that viruses are powerful models for understanding structure-based riboregulation more broadly.

papers.title: Mapping Functional Transitions across Protein Homologues from a Single Simulation: Application of gEDES-HM to Adenylate Kinases.
papers.abstract: Proteins fluctuate across different conformational states, which constitute a dynamic ensemble that regulates their interaction networks and functions. Predicting the conformational landscape remains a computational challenge, and even more difficult is capturing the link between state distributions and specific functions within protein homologues. Here, we present gEDES-HM (generalized Ensemble Docking with Enhanced sampling of pocket Shape-Homology Modeling), a scalable computational protocol enabling us to remap conformational ensembles obtained from enhanced sampling simulations of a singl
papers.journal: Journal of chemical information and modeling
papers.summary: The authors introduce gEDES-HM, a computational protocol that uses enhanced sampling simulations of a single protein to map conformational ensembles onto homologous proteins, enabling prediction of functional transitions across a protein family. They demonstrate this on adenylate kinases, showing that a single simulation can capture state distributions linked to function in multiple homologues. This offers a scalable way to study conformational landscapes and function without running expensive simulations for each homologue.

papers.title: In-silico transcriptomic characterization analysis identifies SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as key biomarkers and therapeutic targets in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a molecularly heterogeneous malignancy requiring reproducible biomarkers and structurally tractable therapeutic targets. We applied an integrated transcriptomic, network, virtual-screening, docking, ADMET, and molecular-dynamics (MD) workflow using GSE8671, GSE14333, and GSE89076. Differential expression analysis (adjusted p < 0.05, |log2FC= ≥ 1) identified 2092 upregulated/9130 downregulated genes in GSE8671, 926/945 in GSE14333, and 2317/1456 in GSE89076. Cross-dataset concordance was highest between GSE8671 and GSE89076 (r = 0.70), with 1040 shared upregulated and
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic datasets from three colorectal cancer cohorts to identify differentially expressed genes, then uses network analysis and structure-based virtual screening to nominate SMAD5, USP2, and CUL4A as candidate biomarkers and drug targets. The work is entirely computational, with no experimental validation of the proposed biomarkers or compounds.

papers.title: Molecular insights into GPR55 modulation reveal an atypical activation mechanism and glycosylation-dependent efficacy regulation.
papers.abstract: GPR55 is a lipid-activated G protein-coupled receptor (GPCR) implicated in metabolism, inflammation, and neurodegeneration. Lysophosphatidylinositol (LPI) species are proposed as endogenous agonists, but progress in understanding GPR55 function has still been limited by suboptimal chemical probes. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of GPR55 in both inactive and active states. The inactive-state structure bound to the inverse agonist CID16020046 facilitated the rational design of an improved in vitro tool compound, BI-8310. Surprisingly, mutation of a glycosylation s
papers.summary: This study presents cryo-EM structures of the lipid receptor GPR55 in both inactive and active states, revealing an atypical activation mechanism. The inactive-state structure enabled rational design of an improved tool compound (BI-8310), and the authors unexpectedly found that glycosylation regulates receptor efficacy. These findings provide a structural basis for understanding GPR55 signaling and for developing better chemical probes.

papers.title: Biochemistry of protozoan Metacaspases: Structure, processing, and inhibition.
papers.abstract: Metacaspases are calcium-dependent cysteine proteases (clan CD, family C14) present in fungi, protozoa, and plants but absent from mammals. Although structurally related to metazoan caspases, they differ in substrate specificity (cleaving after arginine or lysine), calcium-dependent activation, and monomeric architecture. In protozoan parasites such as Trypanosoma brucei, T. cruzi, Leishmania spp., Plasmodium spp., and Toxoplasma gondii, metacaspases regulate programmed cell death, cell cycle progression, protein quality control, differentiation, and virulence. Their absence in humans and esse
papers.summary: This review examines metacaspases, calcium-dependent cysteine proteases found in fungi, protozoa, and plants but not mammals, focusing on their structure, activation processing, and inhibition. In protozoan parasites like Trypanosoma, Leishmania, Plasmodium, and Toxoplasma, these enzymes control programmed cell death, cell cycle progression, protein quality control, differentiation, and virulence. Because humans lack metacaspases, the authors highlight them as promising targets for antiparasitic drug development.

papers.title: A multi-omics computational framework identifies cell-type-specific therapeutic targets and active compounds of Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. against diabetic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is a leading cause of chronic and end-stage kidney disease, and current therapies leave patients at high risk. Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. (TWHF), a traditional Chinese medicine, reduces proteinuria in DKD, but the compounds and molecular targets responsible remain poorly defined. We hypothesized that specific bioactive compounds of TWHF ameliorate DKD through interactions with cell-type-specific molecular targets, thereby modulating inflammatory, immune, and tissue-remodeling pathways involved in disease progression. By integrating transcriptomic analysis, imm
papers.summary: This study integrates transcriptomic and other multi-omics data to identify cell-type-specific molecular targets of the traditional Chinese medicine Tripterygium wilfordii Hook.f. (TWHF) in diabetic kidney disease. The authors then use these targets to predict active compounds that may modulate inflammatory, immune, and tissue-remodeling pathways. The work provides a computational framework linking herbal compounds to cell-type-specific mechanisms in DKD.

papers.title: Structure-guided development of G protein-biased apelin receptor agonists for cardiovascular disease.
papers.abstract: Apelin receptor (APLNR) is a crucial G protein-coupled receptor that plays a central role in cardiovascular homeostasis; therefore, it represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac hypertrophy, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. However, the activation of APLNR simultaneously engages inhibitory G protein (Gi)-mediated protective signaling and β-arrestin pathways that are associated with pathological cardiac remodeling, thereby imposing significant limitations and challenges for the therapeutic development of conventional balanced agonists. Recent
papers.journal: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B
papers.summary: This paper describes the structure-guided design of apelin receptor (APLNR) agonists that preferentially activate protective G protein signaling while avoiding the β-arrestin pathway linked to pathological cardiac remodeling. By exploiting structural knowledge of the receptor, the authors develop biased agonists with potential for treating heart failure, myocardial infarction, and pulmonary arterial hypertension. The work illustrates how biased agonism can be engineered to improve the therapeutic profile of GPCR-targeted cardiovascular drugs.

papers.title: Thermophysically Guided Design of Spray-Dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Microcapsules with Improved Thermal Stability.
papers.abstract: Spray drying and gastrointestinal transit can cause substantial losses in probiotic viability, limiting effective delivery in food applications. This study developed a thermophysically guided framework for the rational design of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules in three sequential stages. First, Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (Ea: 95.4-198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling provided an empirical screening criterion for the preselection of coating materials; the activation energies are apparent values associated with a composite endo
papers.summary: This study presents a three-stage framework for designing spray-dried Lactiplantibacillus plantarum microcapsules, using Kissinger kinetic analysis of eleven biopolymer candidates (activation energies 95.4–198.4 kJ/mol) combined with pH-dependent solubility profiling to preselect coating materials. The approach aims to improve probiotic viability during spray drying and gastrointestinal transit by rationally selecting encapsulating biopolymers based on their thermal properties.

papers.title: Adhesives Inspired by Marine Organisms: Multifunctional Design and Application for Complex Wet/Underwater Environments.
papers.abstract: Achieving strong adhesion in humid or underwater environments is a long-term challenge in materials science. Water molecules form a hydration layer on the substrate surface, blocking effective contact between the adhesive and the interface, leading to the failure of traditional adhesives. The wet adhesion strength of viscoelastic materials is due to the synergistic effect of interfacial chemical bonds and multiscale energy dissipation, but water environment can seriously interfere with this mechanism. In nature, mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms have evolved unique wet adhesion strategi
papers.summary: This review surveys how marine organisms such as mussels, barnacles, and sandcastle worms achieve strong wet adhesion and how these strategies inspire synthetic adhesives for humid and underwater environments. It emphasizes that water forms a hydration layer blocking interfacial contact, and that successful wet adhesion relies on synergistic interfacial chemical bonds plus multiscale energy dissipation. The paper catalogs bioinspired design principles and applications for complex wet conditions.

papers.title: Microbial Rhodopsins: Structural-Functional Mechanisms and the Design of Optogenetic Silencing Tools-With Emphasis on Halorubrum Archaeorhodopsins.
papers.abstract: Microbial rhodopsins are light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a covalent chromophore and adopt a seven-transmembrane α-helical fold. They are widely distributed across archaea, bacteria, algae, and fungi and mediate diverse functions, including light-driven ion transport, light-gated ion conduction, and photosensory signaling. Since the discovery of bacteriorhodopsin in 1971, the microbial rhodopsin family has expanded continuously, and channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics has revolutionized neuroscience by enabling millisecond-scale optical control of neuronal activity. Howeve
papers.summary: This review examines the structural and functional mechanisms of microbial rhodopsins, a diverse family of light-sensitive membrane proteins that use retinal as a chromophore and share a seven-transmembrane helical fold. It highlights how understanding these mechanisms has enabled the engineering of optogenetic tools, with particular emphasis on Halorubrum archaeorhodopsins as a source for developing light-driven silencing (inhibitory) tools for neuroscience.

papers.title: Rational Design of Molecularly Imprinted Nanozymes for Selective Degradation of Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC).
papers.abstract: Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC) is an engineering thermoplastic whose recycling is hindered by its Code-7 classification and environmental BPA leaching. Here, we report water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes for the selective depolymerization of BPA-PC under mild alkaline conditions. Synthesized within cross-linked surfactant micelles, the optimized nanozyme combines shape-complementary BPA-matched pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. Fluorescence titrations with a soluble dansyl-labeled BPA-PC dimer confirm strong subs
papers.summary: This paper reports water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes designed to selectively depolymerize poly(bisphenol A carbonate) under mild alkaline conditions. The optimized nanozyme combines BPA-shaped binding pockets with surface basicity and achieves a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase, with binding confirmed by fluorescence titration using a labeled BPA-PC dimer. The work demonstrates a rational design strategy for enzyme-mimetic catalysts targeting plastic recycling.

papers.title: A Dipeptide Module Substitution-Based Strategy for the Modification and Evaluation of ACE Inhibitory Peptides.
papers.abstract: Food-derived angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory peptide LYPVK exhibits promising potential for application as an important ingredient with a potential antihypertensive effect in functional foods. However, the structure-activity relationship and the rational design strategy for peptide modification remain insufficiently understood. To address this, dipeptide module substitution was employed to modify and investigate the mechanism of this food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide, providing an insight into the structure-activity relationship. Through integration of molecular docking and ac
papers.summary: This study uses a dipeptide module substitution strategy to modify the food-derived ACE inhibitory peptide LYPVK, aiming to clarify its structure-activity relationship and enable rational design of improved antihypertensive peptides. By combining molecular docking with activity assays, the authors identify which dipeptide modules are critical for ACE inhibition and demonstrate how substitutions can tune potency. The work provides a practical framework for engineering food-derived bioactive peptides.

papers.title: Food-Derived Umami Peptides: Linking Candidate Discovery, Experimental Validation, and Food Applications.
papers.abstract: Alternative proteins and cultivated meat increase the need for flavour strategies that maintain savoury quality with less reliance on salt and conventional seasonings. Food-derived umami peptides are promising candidates, but their practical value depends on evidence beyond sequence prediction. With advances in virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted approaches, discovery is expanding from sensory-guided preparation toward candidate-library construction and data-driven prioritization. This review compares food-protein resources and experimental and sequence-based discovery routes, and
papers.summary: This review examines food-derived umami peptides as alternatives for enhancing savory flavor with reduced salt and conventional seasonings, particularly relevant as alternative proteins and cultivated meat gain prominence. It compares discovery approaches ranging from sensory-guided preparation to virtual digestion, peptidomics, and AI-assisted candidate prioritization, emphasizing that practical value requires experimental validation beyond sequence prediction. The review also surveys food-protein resources and links candidate discovery to experimental validation and food applications.

papers.title: Stoichiometry-dependent gating and structural pharmacology of cardiac GIRK1/4 channels.
papers.abstract: Cardiac G protein-gated inwardly rectifying potassium-K + (GIRK) channels, formed by GIRK1/4 heterotetramers or GIRK4 homotetramers, are crucial regulators of heart rate, and their dysfunction is associated with atrial fibrillation. Despite their therapeutic potential as anti-arrhythmic targets, development of selective GIRK modulators has been limited by an incomplete understanding of their structures, gating mechanisms, and pharmacology. Here, we report high-resolution structures of the GIRK4 homotetramer and of GIRK1/4 heterotetramers, revealing that they form in unexpected 1:3 and 2:2 asse
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study presents high-resolution cryo-EM structures of cardiac GIRK channels, revealing that GIRK1/4 heterotetramers assemble in unexpected 1:3 and 2:2 stoichiometries rather than the assumed 2:2 arrangement. The structures show that subunit stoichiometry influences channel gating and pharmacology, providing a structural basis for developing selective anti-arrhythmic modulators targeting atrial fibrillation.

papers.title: PepRePs: Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases Designed with Generative Language Models.
papers.abstract: Phosphorylation is a fast, reversible layer of post-translational control that directly governs protein activity, signaling flux, and cell state. Kinases and phosphatases collectively establish these phosphorylation states, but their dysregulation drives cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and developmental disorders. Selectively manipulating the phosphorylation of individual proteins in cells remains challenging, particularly for disordered substrates. Here, we introduce Peptide-Retargeted Phosphatases (PepRePs), a genetically encoded system that fuses a peptide binder to a serine/threonine p
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce PepRePs, a genetically encoded system that retargets serine/threonine phosphatases to specific substrate proteins by fusing them to peptide binders, enabling selective manipulation of phosphorylation on individual proteins in cells, including disordered substrates. The peptide binders are designed using generative language models, addressing a key challenge in kinase/phosphatase research where selective control of phosphorylation states has been difficult.

papers.title: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation Implicate AKT1-Associated Signaling in the Protective Effects of Panax notoginseng Against Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive and fatal cardiopulmonary disease characterized by pulmonary vascular remodeling, endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and increased pulmonary vascular resistance. Despite advances in targeted therapies, effective treatment options remain limited. This study investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effects of Panax notoginseng against PAH through integrated computational and experimental validation. Network pharmacology was employed to identify the bioactive compounds and therapeutic targets of Panax notoginseng.
papers.summary: This study combines network pharmacology with experimental validation to identify AKT1-associated signaling as a key mechanism by which Panax notoginseng protects against pulmonary arterial hypertension. The work links bioactive compounds from the herb to PAH-relevant targets and provides experimental support for the AKT1 pathway as a mediator of the protective effect.

papers.title: Shexiang Huayu Xingnao Granule Alleviates Intracerebral Hemorrhage via PI3K/AKT-Mediated Neuroinflammation Regulation: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
papers.abstract: Employing network pharmacology prediction combined with experimental validation, this research elucidated the underlying mechanisms of Shexiang Huayu Xingnao granules (SXHY) against intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH).
papers.summary: This study uses network pharmacology predictions combined with experimental validation to show that Shexiang Huayu Xingnao granules alleviate intracerebral hemorrhage by regulating neuroinflammation through the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway. The work identifies a plausible mechanistic basis for a traditional Chinese medicine formulation in treating ICH.

papers.title: Fragment-based active-site exploration of urethane hydrolases reveals a diversity of urethane binding modes.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in the discovery, characterization and engineering of urethanases provide new opportunities for the sustainable biocatalytic degradation of polyurethane waste. A mechanistic understanding of enzyme-plastic interactions is essential for structure-based engineering to enhance urethanase activity. However, the extremely complex and hydrophobic nature of polyurethane makes it challenging to elucidate the structural basis of enzyme-plastic interactions. Here, we used a fragment-based approach to characterize the active sites of two novel urethanases called amidase U11 and esterase A
papers.journal: Acta crystallographica. Section D, Structural biology
papers.summary: This study uses fragment-based crystallography to probe the active sites of two newly identified urethane hydrolases, amidase U11 and esterase A, revealing that urethane binds in multiple distinct orientations. The work provides structural insight into enzyme-plastic interactions that could guide engineering of more efficient urethanases for polyurethane waste degradation.

papers.title: SprintX: mitigating data scarcity in antibody design via synthetic structural prior knowledge dataset.
papers.abstract: Structure-based artificial intelligence (AI)-driven antibody design is increasingly important for therapeutic development, yet progress has been hindered by the scarcity of high-quality antibody-antigen complex structures for model training. To alleviate this bottleneck, we introduce SprintX (Structural Prior for Antibody-Antigen CompleXes), a large-scale AlphaFold3-derived synthetic dataset designed to provide structural prior knowledge for antibody-antigen modeling. Unlike conventional docking-based synthesis pipelines, SprintX uses AlphaFold3 to generate antigen-conditioned candidate comple
papers.summary: SprintX is a large-scale synthetic dataset of antibody-antigen complex structures generated using AlphaFold3, created to address the scarcity of high-quality experimental structures for training AI-based antibody design models. Unlike docking-based approaches, it uses AlphaFold3 to produce antigen-conditioned candidate complexes, providing structural prior knowledge that can be used to pretrain or augment models for antibody-antigen modeling.

papers.title: Aptamers without SELEX: De novo design from protein structure in hours.
papers.abstract: Systematic evolution of ligands by exponential enrichment (SELEX)-based aptamer discovery can be constrained by target availability, selection biases, and optimization requirements. We introduce Xelari, a modular pipeline for de novo DNA and RNA aptamer design from protein structures without target-specific SELEX data or retraining. Xelari combines algorithmic modules with surrogate models trained on physical or structural references. InNA reproduced nucleotide-amino-acid interaction energies with RMSE of 0.19 kcal/mol across 483,735 reference pairs. AliNA achieved a mean F1 of 0.757 on 339 PD
papers.summary: The authors present Xelari, a modular computational pipeline that designs DNA and RNA aptamers de novo directly from protein structures, bypassing experimental SELEX selection entirely. It combines algorithmic modules with surrogate models trained on physical and structural references, reproducing nucleotide-amino-acid interaction energies with low error and achieving solid performance in predicting binding interfaces. This could dramatically accelerate aptamer discovery by removing dependence on target availability and selection biases.

papers.title: UPLC-MS/MS-GNPS based metabolite profiling and inhibitory potential of Vitex negundo L. leaves against Shiga toxins: Applications for biodegradable films with antibacterial properties.
papers.abstract: Antibiotic therapy for STEC O157:H7 infections induces Shiga toxin release, highlighting the need for alternative, food-compatible antimicrobial strategies. The ethanolic leaf extract of Vitex negundo L. was characterized by UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS, integrated with Feature-Based Molecular Networking (GNPS), which putatively annotated 56 metabolites. Computational screening of all annotated compounds against the Stx1 and Stx2 B-subunits identified compound 8, an iridoid glycoside, as the top-ranked candidate with predicted Stx1-binding potential (ΔG = -6.9 kcal/mol; Ki = 8.7 µM). Over 100 ns of molecul
papers.summary: The study characterizes the ethanolic leaf extract of Vitex negundo using UPLC-qTOF-MS/MS and GNPS molecular networking, annotating 56 metabolites. Computational docking and molecular dynamics identify an iridoid glycoside (compound 8) as a top candidate for binding Shiga toxin B-subunits, suggesting a food-compatible strategy to inhibit STEC O157:H7 toxin activity. The work also explores incorporating the extract into biodegradable films with antibacterial properties.

papers.title: Comparative Hydrophobicity Analysis of Human β-Tubulin and Bacterial FtsZ Using the Fuzzy Oil Drop Model: Potential Implications for Chaperone-Assisted Folding.
papers.abstract: The issue of protein folding in vivo remains an unsolved problem despite important progress achieved by artificial intelligence (AlphaFold). Experimental studies have shown that there are several mechanisms involved in this process. The main distinction concerns the involvement of chaperone proteins in this process as opposed to spontaneous folding. Evolutionary analysis shows that tubulin in eukaryotic organisms requires engagement of the ATP-dependent ring-shaped chaperonin TRiC/CCT, while the homologous protein in prokaryotic organisms obtains its functional structure without the support fr
papers.summary: This computational study compares the hydrophobicity distributions of human β-tubulin and its bacterial homolog FtsZ using the Fuzzy Oil Drop model, which describes how hydrophobic residues are organized relative to the protein core. The analysis suggests that differences in hydrophobic core organization may explain why eukaryotic tubulin requires the chaperonin TRiC/CCT for folding while bacterial FtsZ can fold spontaneously. The work offers a structural rationale linking hydrophobicity patterns to chaperone dependence.

papers.title: HNRNPH2-R114W remodels RNA splicing and neurodevelopmental gene programs in isogenic cerebral organoids.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder has been linked to disrupted RNA processing during corticogenesis, yet variant-specific mechanisms remain difficult to resolve. Isogenic cerebral organoids derived from a patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) line carrying the HNRNPH2-R114W variant and its CRISPR-corrected counterpart serve as a human developmental model to investigate variant-associated RNA dysregulation. Imaging quantification and exploratory bulk RNA sequencing, performed at a single developmental time point on a pooled organoid RNA from each genotype, identify coordinated remodeling
papers.summary: Using isogenic cerebral organoids derived from a patient iPSC line carrying the HNRNPH2-R114W variant and its CRISPR-corrected counterpart, the authors show that this autism-linked mutation remodels RNA splicing and alters neurodevelopmental gene expression programs during corticogenesis. Imaging and bulk RNA-seq at a single developmental time point reveal coordinated transcriptomic changes associated with the variant. The work provides a human developmental model for dissecting variant-specific RNA dysregulation in neurodevelopment.

papers.title: Integrated in vitro and in silico assessment of antimicrobial, chemical antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities of endophytic Aspergillus sp. GK1 isolated from Mentha spicata roots.
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants are a source of structurally diverse endophytic fungi which harbor significant pharmaceutical potential.
papers.summary: This study isolated the endophytic fungus Aspergillus sp. GK1 from Mentha spicata roots and characterized its secondary metabolites. Extracts showed antimicrobial, antioxidant, and cytotoxic activities in vitro, and computational (in silico) analyses were used to predict the responsible compounds and their binding to target proteins. The work highlights endophytic fungi from medicinal plants as a source of bioactive natural products for drug discovery.

papers.title: InRegPep: a web server for modeling of parallel beta-sheet fibrillar aggregates of amyloidogenic peptides.
papers.abstract: Predicting the structures of peptide or protein aggregates that assemble into amyloid protofilaments remains one of the most challenging tasks in computational structural biology. Computational difficulties arise mainly from the large size of the modeled systems and the extensive timescales of aggregation processes. The InRegPep web server is designed for the multiscale structural modeling of peptide aggregates that preferentially adopt in-register parallel β-sheet architectures. The method employs the coarse-grained CABS model, which enables the assembly of a large number of aggregates compos
papers.summary: InRegPep is a web server that uses a coarse-grained CABS model to build structural models of amyloidogenic peptides that assemble into in-register parallel β-sheet fibrillar aggregates. It addresses the computational challenge of modeling large aggregate systems by enabling efficient assembly of many peptide chains into protofilament-like architectures.

papers.title: Effectiveness of a hospital intelligent financial system based on AI and RPA.
papers.abstract: Hospital financial management is facing ongoing challenges. Although artificial intelligence (AI) and robotic process automation (RPA) have shown their potential, there is still a lack of empirical evidence of the effectiveness of the integration of the two in the financial operations of hospitals. This study aims to evaluate the application effect of a set of an AI-RPA integrated intelligent financial system in a large hospital in China.
papers.summary: This study evaluates an integrated AI and robotic process automation (RPA) financial system deployed in a large Chinese hospital, aiming to provide empirical evidence on its effectiveness. The abstract indicates the system was assessed for its impact on hospital financial operations, though specific quantitative results are not detailed here. The work addresses a gap in empirical validation of combined AI-RPA approaches in healthcare finance.

papers.title: Tianwang Buxin Dan regulated PI3K/Akt/mTOR signaling pathway to improve constipation and emotional disorders in rats.
papers.abstract: Functional constipation (FC) is frequently comorbid with anxiety and depression, yet pharmacological strategies targeting both gastrointestinal and emotional symptoms remain limited. This study investigated the therapeutic effects and molecular mechanisms of Tianwang Buxin Dan (TWBXD), a classical Chinese herbal formula, in treating FC with emotional disturbances using an integrated strategy combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, and in vivo validation.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the traditional Chinese herbal formula Tianwang Buxin Dan can simultaneously relieve functional constipation and associated anxiety/depression in rats. Using network pharmacology and molecular docking, the authors identify the PI3K/Akt/mTOR pathway as a key mechanism and validate this in vivo, suggesting the formula may treat both gut and emotional symptoms through a shared signaling pathway.

papers.title: Virology-aware artificial intelligence for respiratory antiviral discovery: from molecular docking biases to RdRp-centered benchmarking.
papers.abstract: Respiratory RNA viruses remain a persistent threat because they combine high transmissibility, rapid evolution, immune escape, zoonotic spillover, and incomplete therapeutic coverage. RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and polymerase complexes are among the most conserved and pharmacologically actionable viral targets, yet they are also challenging computational targets because their ligandable states depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions. Artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), geometri
papers.summary: This review argues that AI-driven discovery of antivirals against respiratory RNA viruses must be designed around the specific biology of RNA-dependent RNA polymerases (RdRps) and their polymerase complexes, rather than generic docking pipelines. The authors highlight how standard molecular docking and AI models can be biased by the complex ligandable states of RdRps—which depend on RNA templates, cofactors, divalent metals, multidomain architecture, and conformational transitions—and propose RdRp-centered benchmarking as a more rigorous evaluation framework.

papers.title: Integrative genomic SEM analysis of shared genetic architecture and candidate genes for insulin resistance-related metabolic traits.
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance is a complex metabolic state involving impaired insulin sensitivity, compensatory insulin secretion, abnormal lipid metabolism, and altered fat distribution. However, the shared genetic architecture underlying these correlated phenotypes remains incompletely defined. In this study, we applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling to genome-wide association summary statistics of fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity index, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio to construct an insulin resistance-related latent genetic factor. SNP-level association analysis was then performed for
papers.summary: This study used genomic structural equation modeling on GWAS summary statistics for fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity index, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio to construct a latent genetic factor representing insulin resistance. The authors then performed SNP-level association analysis to identify shared genetic architecture and candidate genes underlying these correlated metabolic traits. The work provides a framework for understanding the common genetic basis of insulin resistance-related phenotypes.

papers.title: Structure-based minimization of a high-mobility group protein B1 (HMGB1) B box peptide uncouples anti-NETotic activity and anti-biofilm function.
papers.abstract: We previously showed that human HMGB1 has anti-biofilm activity localized to a 97-amino-acid B-Box-derived peptide (mB Box-97), engineered with a C106S mutation to reduce HMGB1's proinflammatory properties while retaining anti-biofilm function. This peptide also suppresses NETosis by inhibiting neutrophil protein kinase C (PKC) activity. Here, we tested whether the anti-biofilm and anti-NETotic activities of mB Box-97 could be separated into distinct shorter peptides by constructing truncated variants containing Helix 1 of the B-Box (with the C106S mutation), with or without the A Box-B Box li
papers.summary: The authors truncated the HMGB1 B-box peptide (mB Box-97) into shorter variants containing Helix 1 with the C106S mutation, testing whether its anti-biofilm and anti-NETosis activities could be separated. They found that these two functions can be uncoupled into distinct shorter peptides, suggesting the anti-NETotic and anti-biofilm effects are mediated by separable structural elements.

papers.title: Unleashing the industrial potential of microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes: recent advances in protein engineering.
papers.abstract: Plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (PCWPEs) used in industry are predominantly of microbial origin. Key enzyme classes, including cellulases, lytic polysaccharide monooxygenases (LPMOs), β-xylanases, β-mannanases and pectinases, have attained technological maturity and are widely deployed across agro-waste biorefineries, food and feed processing, textile and pulp manufacturing. Low catalytic efficiency, insufficient thermostability, poor operational adaptability, restricted functionality, and product inhibition limit the industrial use of these enzymes. Structure- and sequence-gu
papers.summary: This review surveys recent protein engineering advances aimed at improving microbial plant cell wall polysaccharide-degrading enzymes (cellulases, LPMOs, xylanases, mannanases, pectinases) for industrial use. It highlights how structure- and sequence-guided engineering strategies address key limitations such as low catalytic efficiency, poor thermostability, and product inhibition. The paper consolidates progress toward more robust, industrially viable biocatalysts for biorefineries, food/feed processing, textiles, and pulp manufacturing.
